<result>**Recommendation.** Do not create P-research-ops. P-research (26 open B-rw-* tasks) and P-research-flows (31 open RF-* tasks, RF-decide done) already hold about 85% of what the operator asked for. File 14 RS-* tasks as extensions of those two phases, with 4 optional RS-sci-* science tasks. Three things come first: make the research gate bind (B-rw-gate-link), add an evidence-type taxonomy with extra verdict states, and add clean-checkout re-run of probes. The scientific/genetics profile stays an optional pack. I read "genetic" as "generic" (domain-agnostic first), since a genetics-only reading would leave the engineering, math and literature work unmanaged. Of the 14 tasks, 13 are Wave 3 or later, because they depend on unbuilt B-rw-* and RF-* work, so the near-term value is ordering that work, not adding to it.

All figures come from the event-log snapshot in my worktree, which ends 2026-10-29. `ddflow research list` shows notes dated up to 2026-11-03, so main has newer events. Counts are therefore lower bounds. Grades: [V] means I measured or fetched it; [K] means from memory.

## Part 1. What we have and plan

**1a. Existing research machinery [V]**
- **Note record.** `ddflow research add` takes question, claim, mechanism, falsifier, probe, probe_output, verdict, sources (a list of strings), budget and item. Source: `[REDACTED:path]`.
- **What is enforced.** Verdict must be CONFIRMED, REFUTED or THEORETICAL. CONFIRMED and REFUTED need a non-empty probe. Falsifier, mechanism and sources are not enforced.
- **No revision.** There is no supersede, update or expiry verb for a note. No note was ever re-recorded (0 updated subjects), and only `--merge-into` appends.
- **Research gate.** The `research` gate is an agent gate at position 1. It is not required, needs no evidence and has no reviewer. Its prompt says "state claim, mechanism, falsifier, cheapest test, paste command AND output". Nothing checks that a record exists. 1258 passes and 59 skips were recorded, and the single `gate.failed` event for the research gate is not attributed. B-rw-gate-link plans the check.
- **Pipeline for `kind=research`.** It gets the full task pipeline: research, rules, implement, rubber_duck, critic, standards, ci, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, merge. Only an all-docs diff falls to `doc_pipeline` via `doc_pipeline_paths`. The doc pipeline (rules, implement, standards, dedupe, merge) has no rubber_duck, critic or independence requirement, so a doc-only research task skips independent review.
- **Dedupe.** `research_task_asks` defaults to false: a note against a task is listed, not blocking. Note-against-note uses `ask_threshold`.
- **Researcher agent.** The definition is `ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md`. It is read-only and has WebFetch and WebSearch. It cannot claim items, so it cannot hold a research task, run a scratch worktree or run a benchmark. It files notes by CLI.
- **Managed docs.** There are 55 files in `docs/ddflow/research/`. `deep-research.md` (2026-10-18) states plainly that using agents' native search is NOT COVERED and that a research critic and claim panel are PARTLY covered.

**Measured on 1274 notes (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-29)** [V]

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|

## Part 3. Gaps and design

**Reading used.** Generic first, because the tasks in P-research-flows are domain-agnostic. Science is an optional pack.

**Research kinds and evidence required (extension 1)**

| Kind | Evidence that should count |
|---|---|
| Literature/tech survey | cited: URL, quote, retrieval date, Admiralty-style grade; PRISMA-style counts |
| Programming (library/algorithm comparison, benchmark, spike, root-cause, performance) | executable: pinned command, env fingerprint, seeds, variance across N runs, raw output blob |
| Engineering (feasibility, design alternatives, measurements) | executable measurements plus a decision (D-) with a reasoned alternatives table |
| Scientific | pre-registered plan, effect size with interval, multiple-comparison correction recorded, data hash, no p-hacking by repetition (count of attempts is itself recorded) |
| Math | proved (Lean/Coq/Isabelle kernel check), SMT-decided (Z3 result plus a reproducible script), CAS-derived (SymPy/Sage script), numerically tested (stated range and tolerance), conjecture. The claim must record which level, since "tested numerically" must never read as "proved". RF-flow-math checks the statement text as well, because a compiling proof of a drifted statement is the named failure. |

**Evidence-type ledger (extension 2).** Each claim carries `evidence_type`: executable, cited or reasoned. Each type has its own verification path.
- **Executable.** A command ddflow re-runs on a clean checkout in a scratch worktree and compares the output digest. Fail-before: if the probe passes on the unfixed baseline the claim is vacuous (the QA-f2p-task idea applied to claims). This extends B-rw-checks.
- **Cited.** A second agent re-fetches the source and confirms the quote is present (B-rw-sources plus RF-audit).
- **Reasoned.** An independent reviewer under D-reviewer-independence-soft tiers (family, then model fallback, author never). It is recorded as the lowest rung.

**Verdict states.** Keep CONFIRMED/REFUTED/THEORETICAL as the headline verdict, which existing tooling depends on. Add an orthogonal `strength` field (asserted / supported / verified, as RF-confidence already defines) plus an `evidence_mark` of PROVED, REPLICATED or STALE. Do not extend the verdict enum. The 1274 existing notes and every filter assume three values, and a derived mark avoids a migration. STALE is computed from a `review_by` date, not entered.

**Known failure modes to guard.** Fabricated citations (fetch-and-quote), misreported numbers (every number tied to a run id, RF-audit), p-hacking by repetition (RF-stop counts attempts; require the number of trials in the note), unverifiable "proofs" (kernel check or labelled THEORETICAL), and fetched pages treated as instructions (see safety).

**Research for another project, and research as a project (extension 3).** A standalone research project is a normal ddflow project whose phase chain is scoping, collection, analysis, synthesis, review, report, built from RF-template stages. Research for another project reuses XP-target-project: the target project's records get read-only access plus the findings written back as a note and a decision proposal, never as edits. Deliverables (report, dataset pointer, notebook, proof artifact) become `doc` items with their own review. A report with no verified claims links fails the audit.

**Safety.** Fetched pages are untrusted data: each tool result is stored with `trust=unknown` in a `<ddflow-record>`-style fence and cannot become an instruction. Web access needs consent (RF-native-policy). Cost caps come from P-safeguards.envelope. For science: redaction rules so sample or patient data and genomic data never enter the event log, which is committed, so data stays outside git with a hash pointer only.

**Programming research (extension 4).** Experiments run in scratch worktrees via the same `ddflow run` machinery as RF-run, with PM-* variance control (N repetitions, noise band, env fingerprint), and results kept as evidence blobs under `.ddflow/blobs`. A result inside the noise band must be recorded as no-effect, not as a win.

## BDD and specification by example

- **Cucumber [V].** Its guidance (https://cucumber.io/docs/bdd/better-gherkin/): declarative scenarios describe behaviour, imperative UI scripts are tightly coupled to the UI and cost more to maintain, and a declarative style works better as living documentation.

## ATDD, TDD and test-first

- **ATDD and FitNesse [K].** Executable acceptance criteria. ddflow's equivalent is US-verify plus cards.
- **TDD evidence [V].** Fucci et al. 2016, a multi-site blind replication, found no significant TDD versus test-last difference in testing effort (p=.27), external quality (p=.82) or productivity (p=.83). A 2020 critique summarised six meta-analyses as quality "no difference to improvement" and productivity "inconclusive to degradation". A 2025 study found only 3% of primary studies appear in all eight SLRs. Sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.09863 and https://neverworkintheory.org/2016/10/05/test-driven-development.html. I only saw summaries, so check the papers before citing effect sizes.
- **What that means for ddflow.** Do not require TDD as an ideology. Offer a `tdd` pipeline kind as an option for a task or project, and make the red step produce evidence of the right failure (assertion versus ImportError, a distinction R-qa-gate measured). Cost: low. Hype: high.

## 1. Test cases as records

Recommendation: no new "test case" kind. A test case is a **TF-card** (one file, front matter with claim or criterion id, kind, environment and SUT pin) that carries a `runs:` list of pytest node ids, commands or URLs. Code stays the source of truth: the card is the specification and the code is the executable. A manual case has no `runs:` and is executed by a person or card-runner agent, producing step results (pass, fail, blocked, skipped), evidence blobs (stored by hash, secrets scrubbed) and the tester's identity. This is TM-case-manual, a thin extension of TF-card-run. Borrow Kiwi's detail that an execution records the case-text version it ran against.

## 2. Spec to test derivation

- **Chain.** Story criteria (US-criteria) or spec sections (SPEC-*) feed a planner step that drafts cards. Each draft carries `covers: S#n` and is unconfirmed (as PD-trace requires for LLM-proposed links) until a second family reviewer confirms. Cards promote to code via TF-promote.
- **Encodes-the-spec check.** It is not an LLM opinion. It is a probe: does the test fail when the criterion is violated? Use a mutant or a spec-violating stub that ddflow executes (same rule as D-qa-evidence-answers: findings without a probe are advisory). TF-lens covers the review prompt; the probe is the new part.
- **Gherkin.** Optional export only (see Part 2).

## 3. TDD

A `tdd` kind pipeline: `red` (new tests fail before, recorded with failure kind) then `implement` (green) then `refactor` (tests unchanged, QA-weakening clean) then `merge`. QA-f2p-task supplies the red measurement. TM-tdd adds the pipeline, the failure-kind rule (an ImportError-only red is flagged weak) and an outside-in variant whose first test is an acceptance card. It is optional per task because TDD's measured benefit is inconclusive [V].

## 4. Test runs as first-class records

TF-record already specifies result, repeats, seed, SUT pin, environment id and tool versions, with a hash-plus-summary rule for the log and raw output in a file. PM-env-fingerprint is done and gives the fingerprint. Nothing new except trend reporting, which TM-reports and PM-report-* provide.

## 5. Reports

Managed document types, rendered through PM-report-data and PM-report-text, on demand (`ddflow test report <kind>`) and as a periodic job (P-schedule):

- test summary;
- defect report;
- traceability matrix (TM-matrix);
- coverage by risk;
- release readiness, where each exit criterion is a check evaluated like RQM-check (TM-gonogo).

A criterion that cannot run is "unavailable", never passed. Go/no-go acceptance is person-only, like US-accept.

## 6. QA-as-a-project mode

A ddflow project with its own queue and event log:

- **Target pointer.** `[target]` names a repo path or URL and a ref, in `readonly` (checkout at the pinned sha) or `worktree` mode, with the target's hooks disabled. Every record carries the SUT pin (TF-pin vocabulary). The SUT sha is stamped on each run.
- **Roles.** Tester, QA lead and test reviewer. Permissions: a tester may add tests, run suites and file defects, but not edit target product code unless the QA lead grants it. Enforce with lease globs (tester's globs = `qa/**` or the target's `tests/**`), and TF-readonly's diff gate once it lands. B-sub-defaults already specifies "tester limited to test globs".
- **Findings.** Bug records in the QA project with a `target` field, exported as files or pushed to the target's forge (TM-defect-forge, via ADP-forge). The forge is the system of record for the target team; ddflow does not become their tracker.
- **Assessment tasks.** Charters, risk assessment, security review and deployment readiness, shipped as an SE-packs pack.
- **Evidence collection.** All blobs hashed and referenced from records, never in the event log.

Alternative placement: the QA project can live inside the target repo, using the ordinary queue. TM-qa-profile should work in both.

## 7. Deployment and infrastructure assessment

Checks through ADP-tools, never a new engine, each recorded unavailable when the tool is absent:

- hadolint for Dockerfiles;
- tflint, Checkov or `trivy config` for IaC;
- kubeconform for Kubernetes manifests;
- conftest for policy;
- post-deploy smoke, which is TF-flows-ops;
- rollback verification and DR drill records;
- a drift job using `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` or `helm diff`.

TK-detect finds the stack and TK-propose offers the tools with consent.

## 8. DevSecOps

- **Scanners.** SAST, SCA, secrets and SARIF map to SEC-scanners, TK-sarif and SEC-deps; they are not repeated here.
- **New: supply-chain evidence.** Syft or Trivy to CycloneDX 1.7, a stored digest, and verification of SLSA provenance and sigstore attestations (verify only).
- **New: DAST.** ZAP baseline or Schemathesis against a sandbox endpoint, behind TM-safety.
- **New: compliance evidence pack.** Control to check to latest evidence at a sha, mapped to SSDF v1.1 and ASVS.
- **New: threat records.** STRIDE threat records linked to mitigations and tests, on top of SEC-threatmodel's inventory.

## 9. Metrics

`found_in` (dev gate, QA cycle, after merge, production) lets ddflow compute escape rate and DRE per phase. DORA-like numbers come from existing events: lead time (claim to merge), change fail rate (fix-after-merge, already in PM-quality-signals), recovery time (bug open to fixed). Test effectiveness is bugs caught by a cycle versus found later. Extend PM-quality-signals; do not add a second metrics module.

## 10. Safety

- **Environment classes.** `sandbox | ci | staging | prod-like | production`, each with a consent grade. An agent never touches production-like or production without a recorded human grant (D-test-flows already requires this for chaos, production-touching and hardware).
- **Egress allowlist** per environment; resource and time budgets per run; destructive-command denylist.
- **Test data.** Synthetic only; secrets by reference through P-secrets and never in evidence; gitleaks over stored evidence blobs.
- **Prompt injection.** Test output, logs and fetched web pages are untrusted. Reuse the `<ddflow-record trust=...>` convention and SPEC-inject's fencing for imported content, and the SEC-sandbox for reproducers.

1. Do you want QA-as-a-project mode as a first-class profile (separate project against a target, plus the in-target variant)? **Default:** yes, both, starting with TM-target.

# Change management for ddflow: research findings and proposed phase P-change-mgmt (R-change-mgmt)

## Recommendation

1. Build change management as a derived view and report over records ddflow already writes, not as a new tracker. A single change record joins `item.completed` (approval, forced, overridden, sha, ledger), the `ask.*` events, gates, `ci.result`, `bug.found.item` and decision links.
2. Ship a new phase `P-change-mgmt` with 20 tasks, and **use the prefix `CHG-`, not `CM-`**. `CM-` already names about 24 commit-message tasks (CM-packs, CM-lint and so on), and `GP-org` depends on `CM-packs-diff`.
3. The data supports a lean model. A DORA-style one (peer review plus the automated gate pipeline, standard changes pre-authorised, a risk class that scales approvals) fits ddflow, and a board-style CAB does not.
4. Measured in this log, 0 of 312 approvals were denied, 16.5% of completions were forced, and config changes leave no event. The first value is therefore evidence shown with each approval, a risk class, a rollback field, config history and a report. Enforcement (freeze windows, required rollback plans) comes only after a measured advisory period.
5. Eight tasks can start today. Cross-project change management (a project acting for another project) waits behind long chains: CN-cr needs CN-consumers, CN-spec-kind and SE-kind-data/CN-manifest. XP-target-project and the MR-* tasks are not filed, so I describe them as proposed ids.

## Operator questions (with recommended defaults)

1. **Prefix.** `CM-` is taken by commit-message tasks. Use `CHG-`? Default: yes.
2. **Scope of enforcement.** Advisory (report only) for one release, then blocking by class? Default: advisory first, measure false positives, then flip per check like `QA-defaults`.
3. **Class model.** Three ITIL classes, or fold emergency into a tag on normal? Default: three classes. Emergency requires an after-the-fact review item.
4. **Standard changes.** Which pre-approved types? Default: docs-only, upgrade-note regeneration, baseline-red accept, patch dependency bumps. All limited to low risk, with evidence present and a notice sent.
5. **Rollback plan.** Required for high risk, optional otherwise, and does `ddflow revert` run automatically after red main? Default: required for high risk only. Revert is manual-triggered, not automatic.
6. **Freeze windows.** Do you want them at all, and who may override? Default: opt-in config, off by default, override needs a person's T2 approval, emergency class passes with after-review.
7. **Approval fatigue.** Zero denials in 312 answers. Do you want sampling audits and an evidence view on every request, and should the standing window keep the 24 h cap? Default: yes to both, and keep the cap.
8. **Cross-project.** Should ddflow act as the change manager for another project now? Default: wait for `CN-cr` and the unfiled `XP-target-project`. Meanwhile record the intent as a link only.

Each entry shows the grade, what it does, what ddflow could borrow, cost, and hype.

**Monorepo tooling**
- **Nx** [V] (nx.dev/docs/features/ci-features/affected, fetched 2026-11-03): diffs against a base commit, selects tasks whose declared inputs changed, and its limits are undeclared inputs and lock-file changes.

- **west** [V] (Zephyr manifest docs): a manifest pins a revision per project, imports others, and `west manifest --freeze` rewrites revisions to SHAs.

  - Borrow: no new transport. Submodule pointer-bump pairing is already CN-umbrella-submodule.
  - Pitfall: submodules go stale silently, and detached HEAD plus recursion hurt agents.
- **Copybara** [V] (github.com/google/copybara README): transforms and moves code between repos; one repo must be authoritative; git only.
  - Borrow: the authoritative-side rule for generated or mirrored artifacts.
  - Skip: implementing transformations.
- **Sourcegraph Batch Changes** [V] (sourcegraph.com/docs/batch_changes): a batch spec produces changeset specs; a controller reconciles pull requests with status, checks, review and a burndown; Enterprise plan.

- **Renovate and Dependabot** [V partial]:
  - Dependabot groups updates into one PR; has `multi-ecosystem-groups`; cooldown defaults to 3 days and excludes security updates. Cross-directory grouping needs `group-by: dependency-name` and one ecosystem.
  - Renovate automerge is "without human intervention". Its other options were not fetched; the page was truncated.

- **Zuul** [V] (zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html, latest, v14.3.0):
  - Changes are queued in shared queues across repos and each is tested as if the changes ahead of it had merged.
  - `Depends-On` is a one-way DAG across repos and even across systems; dependencies are enqueued ahead of dependents.
  - A failed change is dropped and the rest are retested.
  - Each queue item freezes repo state.
  - Borrow: this is the model for the MR joint gate and landing order.
  - Cost: moderate, since we need no CI server.
  - Hype: low; it is proven at OpenStack scale.

Ranking is value/effort. "Exists" means shipped.

**1. Manifest.** Extend CN-manifest's `.ddflow/constellation.toml`.
- Add a location that is either a local path or a forge URL, plus roles and relation edges.
- A relation looks like `provides = [{contract = "api/openapi.yaml"}]` and `consumes = [{from = "svc", contract = "...", pin = {file = "...", regex = "..."}}]`.
- Pins read like `[flow.version_files]` (path to a regex with one capture group), which already exists. That makes drift mechanical.
- Migrate `[schedule] repos` into the manifest with an alias.
- Roles are data entries; AI-roles and CN-roles add entries rather than a second vocabulary.
- Policy inheritance should go through the org layer (a member names an org source). Do not add a new constellation layer, because D-config-layer-order is binding.

**2. Change set.** A data-declared kind (SE-kind-data is done).
- Fields: id (this can double as the forge topic), intent, members `{repo, item, role, order}`, a Depends-On DAG (cycles refused), origin chain with hop count, a state machine (draft, planned, running, joint-testing, landing, landed, partial, aborted), and a frozen SHA tuple.
- It differs from a CR: a CR is "owner changed a contract, consumers adapt" (one to many, consumer's choice). A change set is "we change this together". A CR's adoption items can become change set members.
- Per-repo items stay in their own repo's log under that repo's own rules. The set holds only references and digests.

**Joint gate.**
- Build a throwaway integration workspace with each member at its frozen head and the rest at their pin.
- Run the declared joint command (the tests repo's suite, or a compose job) through the existing gate runner.
- The result is valid only for that SHA tuple (the same idea as Zuul's frozen queue item). Any head moving invalidates it.
- Speculative order: test each member on top of those ahead of it in the DAG.
- Landing is a saga, not an atomic commit:
  - Land in topological order, each through its own `merge` or `pr` flow.
  - On partial failure, stop the line, set `partial`, and offer forward-fix, revert items (in reverse order, as new reviewed items), or hold.
  - Never auto-revert.
  - Resume must be idempotent.

**3. Impact analysis.**
- Chain: changed paths in A, then contract globs in the manifest, then consumer edges, then inferred edges (lockfiles, imports), then a ranked list marked declared or inferred.
- Break class comes from pluggable checks (oasdiff, buf breaking) through ADP-tools. An unavailable tool is reported `unavailable`, never "no break".
- Identity is a git blob hash for the MVP. CN-digest (model digest, wave 13) comes later.

**4. Sync actions.**
- Never a silent push. Modes per target: `none`, `propose` (default), `worktree`.
- `propose` goes through the forge (PR or issue with the set id and a `Depends-On` footer, under the person's login) or, for a local sibling, through the target's own ddflow CLI. The latter is XP-target-project.
- Reuse the suggestion engine's transport (LK-sg-send/remote). Cross-repo is "suggestion to a project".
- The `worktree` mode is the same as XP-target-project, plus the set's ordered claim: claim in topological order and release everything on the first refusal.

**5. Drift.** A scheduled report, never auto-fix. It covers:
- pins versus the provider's current state;
- contract hashes;
- generated artifacts (the generator command plus a hash);
- docs links;
- lock and advisory freshness (SEC-deps);
- stale `external.observed`.
Findings go to the owning repo's review inbox as items, deduped by a finding digest.

**6. Views.**
- `constellation status|brief|waves` over the union of items, which `external.py` already folds.
- Cross-repo notices ("repo X merged a change that affects you") are read-based first, delivered through the inbox door.
- ETA and cost sum the existing forecast and metrics per member.

**7. Release.**
- A `constellation freeze` lock: repo, SHA or tag, contract digest. This is the BOM, as in `west --freeze`.
- Coordinated version bumps use each member's `flow.version_files` in DAG order.
- Changelogs are aggregated per member.
- The matrix rows come from joint-gate results (CN-matrix later).

**8. Followers.**
- A `follows` relation with `tracks` globs. A code change in those globs raises candidate test items in the tests repo and stale-doc findings in the docs repo.
- A research repo feeds decisions to the code repo as a decision proposal (RS-xproject, read-only target).

**9. Remote and MCP.**
- Keep one MCP server per project. Add a read-only `constellation` action family that reads siblings through one backend: local path, git mirror (CN-mirror), or forge read (ADP-forge, wave 0).
- Writes always go to the target's own server or the forge.
- No-shell parity is required (r-no-shell): every MR verb gets a CLI, MCP and plain-prompt surface.

**10. Safety.**
- Dry-run is the default and blast-radius caps are knobs (max repos per set, max items per run).
- Consent: per-target and operator-only, expiring, using the existing grant and approvals engines. An agent cannot raise its own consent.
- Secrets: nothing is carried in payloads beyond references, with the upstream redaction profile and egress allowlist applied. Forge calls use the person's login; ddflow holds no token.
- Loop guard: the set id, hop count and origin digest travel with every proposal. A→B→A is refused if the set already has an open member in that repo for that cause. The idempotency key is (set, repo, kind, digest).
- Partial-failure recovery is the saga above.
- Sibling text (item titles, spec text) is untrusted data: fence it as imported and scan it (CN-spec-fence, wave 11, applies later).

## Operator questions, with recommended defaults

1. **Phase placement.** New thin `P-constellation-ops` extending P-constellation (default), or append the MR- tasks to P-constellation.
2. **Cross-repo write model.** Proposals only: forge PR or issue under the person's login, or the target's own ddflow (default). Direct local worktree writes into a sibling are off unless granted per target, with expiry.
3. **Where the joint gate runs.** The tests repo as integrator (default), a dedicated integration repo, or the code repo.
4. **Strictness.** Impact and drift findings warn, as D-constellation says (default). The joint gate blocks landing for members of a declared change set only. Do you accept that carve-out?
5. **Partial failure.** Stop the line, then offer forward-fix, revert items, or hold, with no auto-revert (default), or auto-revert already-landed members.
6. **Policy sharing.** Through the org layer only (P-org-config) (default), or add a constellation-level layer. The latter would amend D-config-layer-order.
7. **`[schedule] repos`.** Migrate into the manifest with an alias, read-only meanwhile (default), or keep both.
8. **Scope of reads.** Local sibling paths only first, with the mirror and forge reads from MR-remote-mode later (default). Say if the remote sister projects exist today.

## PART 2 – What others do

### Standards [K, ISO pages returned 403]
- **ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017** (software life-cycle processes) and **15288:2023** (systems) define processes, not phases.
- **29148:2018** (requirements engineering) names the needs → requirements → verification chain and the quality attributes of one requirement: singular, unambiguous, verifiable.
- **42010:2022** (architecture description) defines viewpoints and stakeholder concerns.
- **29119** parts 1–5 cover test processes, documentation and techniques.

Takeaway for ddflow: the standards agree on *what handoff artifact each stage owes the next* and on bidirectional traceability, not on a phase order. That supports a profile-selects-stages design.

### Lifecycle models and platforms [K unless marked]
- **V-model and CMMI:** every left-side artifact has a named right-side verification. Strongest traceability, heaviest.
- **Scrum, Kanban, Shape Up:** small batches and WIP limits; DoR/DoD per stage.
- **DORA capabilities [V, fetched 2026-11-03]:** the page lists process capabilities that map onto ddflow's design. These include working in small batches, work-in-process limits, visibility of work in the value stream, documentation quality, customer feedback and streamlining change approval. Technical ones include test automation, trunk-based development and monitoring. The DORA 2025 page [V] says "AI's primary role is as an amplifier, magnifying an organization's existing strengths and weaknesses." That page gave no numbers.
- **Team Topologies / SRE handoffs** [K]: explicit team interfaces and production-readiness reviews are a stage gate.
- **Jira + Confluence + Xray, Codebeamer, Polarion, Jama** [K]: ALM tools with typed requirement-test-defect links. Polarion documents "suspect links" (what makes one suspect, how it is cleared) [V, only the page summary was readable].
- **Azure DevOps** [V, page ms.date 2026-02-28]: typed work-item links (Parent/Child, Predecessor/Successor, Related, Consumes From/Produced For across orgs); orphan queries such as unparented stories and "items with no linked commits or PRs" are built in. Test Plans, Suites and Cases cannot be queried in a parent-child tree, only through direct-links queries.
- **GitLab Value Stream Analytics** [K; fetch redirected to auth]: stage times over issue → plan → code → test → review → deploy. This is the model for LF-pm-view.
- **GitHub Copilot coding agent** [V]: one branch and one PR per task, firewall allowlists honored, sessions cap at 59 minutes in Actions mode, custom instructions/agents/skills/MCP. The page does not describe approval rules, so I cannot say who approves the PR.

Failure modes with evidence:
- **Spec-code and review overload** [V, Fowler/Böckeler, 2025-10-15]: Kiro produced 4 stories and 16 criteria for a small bug; markdown review "can be more burdensome than reviewing code"; spec-kit regenerated existing classes as duplicates in one case; one workflow does not fit all sizes.
- **Productivity illusion** [V, METR 2025-07-10]: 16 developers, 246 issues; 19% *slower* with AI; they expected -24% time and afterwards believed -20%. METR now says these early-2025 results are out of date, so treat it as a warning on self-assessment, not as a current rate.
- **End-to-end tasks** [V partial]: SWE-Lancer (arXiv 2502.12115, 2025-02-17, v4 2025-05-29) has 1,400+ Upwork tasks worth about $1M and says frontier models cannot solve the majority; the page gives no per-model figures.
- Requirements drift, test gaming, documentation rot, role confusion and cost blow-up are all plausible from the sources above, but I have **no measured rate** for any of them [K]. Anthropic's 15x token figure is the only cost number fetched.

Human-team effectiveness [V from the DORA list]: small batches, WIP limits, visible work, fast feedback and streamlined (not skipped) change approval. DORA's claim that AI amplifies the existing system supports building the handoff checks first.

Hype ranking (my judgement, not measured):
1. **Real and cheap:** spec files as shared context (Kiro/Spec Kit/BMAD); subagent isolation and tool allowlists; wave-parallel tasks from a dependency graph.
2. **Real but oversold:** role-play SOP teams (MetaGPT/ChatDev), because MAST puts failures at misalignment and verification, not in role count.
3. **Unproven:** spec-as-source (Tessl), and "autonomous software engineer" end-to-end claims.

### (a) Lifecycle profile
- **Today:** per-kind pipelines via `[gates].kind_pipelines` (kinds task, phase, bug, doc, research, job), `doc_pipeline`, `phase_pipeline` (research, tasks, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, live_test, corrections, docs, merge in the listing above) and `ddflow flow` for branching.
- **Planned:** SE-workflow-template (templates generate gates), SE-packs (packs off until enabled, D-packs-consent), GC-packs, D-company-workflows (everything configurable per company), RF-template, IA-pack, CN-workflows.
- **Gap:** nothing selects *which stages, artifacts, roles and gates a project uses as a whole*. A profile is a pack: `{stages on/off, kind_pipelines overrides, required artifact kinds, DoR/DoD refs, roles, docs obligations}`.
- **Shipped profiles:** agile-iterative, V-model-regulated (all links mandatory, baselines), kanban-flow, research-only, ops-only, docs-only.
- **Constraint:** the profile may tighten, never silently loosen, company floors (D-config-layer-order, "company enforced" layer).

### (b) Stage gates
Today's phase pipeline gates are code-quality gates, not lifecycle gates.
- **Missing:** a gate type that evaluates *entry and exit checks declared by the owning tracks*. For example: requirements have sources, stories ready, spec approved, tests derived, evidence passed, acceptance given, security passed, release readiness.
- **Mechanism:** `WP-gate-stages` (series-parallel stages) is the host. Each owning track registers a check; the stage gate only aggregates.
- **Person-only sign-offs** already exist as concepts (US-accept, TM-gonogo, PD-source). The stage gate must record an `unavailable` check as unavailable, never as passed.

### (c) Traceability graph
- One read model over typed edges, plus the health metrics: orphan requirements, untested criteria, undocumented features, unreleased changes, decisions without owner, and suspect links.
- **Single primitive:** `PD-trace` (parent content hash at last review) owns suspect marking. `RQM-trace`, `US-trace`, `SPEC-trace` and `TM-matrix` all say to use it.
- **Defect in the ordering:** `RQM-trace` has `needs=['RQM-check']` only and `SPEC-trace` has `needs=['SPEC-bind','RQM-trace']`. Neither depends on `PD-trace`, so "share it, do not fork" is not enforced by order. `PD-trace` itself needs `PD-req-kind`, `TF-trace`, `B-rw-claims`. Add `PD-trace` as a need to both, or declare one common primitive task.
- **Unowned:** the *combined* chain view and the missing edges (defect → release → deployment → incident). That is LF-trace-view and LF-trace-edges.

## Part 2: The extension contract

### Layout and discovery

- A feature is `ddflow/features/<name>.toml`: data only, parsed with `tomllib`, so it costs no import. Code is referenced by `"pkg.mod:attr"` through the existing `Lazy`.
- Discovery is a sorted scan of that directory. A duplicate id raises `DuplicateName`. This is the same discipline as `SECTION_NAMES` and the ports scan.
- Keep the existing per-domain directories (`config_sections/`, `templates/events/`, `templates/kinds/`, `declared/`, `harnesses/`). A feature manifest only wires; it does not replace them.
- Every manifest carries `contract = 1`. A manifest with an unknown contract is skipped and reported. It is never a crash.

### (a) Gate plugin registry

A gate is a `[[gate]]` table with the existing `GateDef` fields, so `tomlcfg.overlay_table` can load it as a new lowest layer. New fields: `check` (the gate kind), `inputs`, `cost` (an estimate, feeds the optimizer cost term), `tier` (independence tier) and `join_role`.

`check` selects a registered runner. Runner kinds: `command`, `probe`, `reviewer`, `rule`, `human`, `composite`. When `check` is absent it is inferred from the old fields, so every existing config behaves the same.

- **command**: the existing `run_command_gate`.
- **probe**: a command whose output is a typed probe record. QA and LK use this.
- **reviewer**: today's `reviewer` field, which keeps independence checks.
- **rule**: evaluates a registered predicate over the item and records the result.
- **human**: today's `human` flag. Its guard (no MCP tool records it, and a committed human gate cannot be unset by the local layer) must stay.
- **composite**: sub-gates under a join policy.

A runner returns the existing outcome set. Anything that could not run is `unavailable`, never `passed`.

### (b) Join policies as data

`[[stage]] id, gates, join` becomes the WP-gate-stages model. A join policy is a pure function `(outcomes, ctx) -> JoinResult(settled, failed, reason)`.

Policies shipped: `all` (the default, today's behaviour), `any_of`, `quorum:N`, `first_failure_stops`, `by_class:<predicate>`. A `weighted` policy is not shipped (see YAGNI below).

Rules that keep it safe:

- A join can change only through a recorded per-item plan revision (WP-plan-record).
- Required gates still bind regardless of the join, as `B-na-required-gate` established for `applies_when`.
- A merged gate keeps its own outcome and note.
- Tighten-only: a feature may add a stricter join. Loosening needs an approval.

### (c) Optimizer providers

`Provider(name, kind, version, schema, weight_knob, cap, explain, fn)` with `kind` one of `signal`, `constraint`, `cost-term`, `resource`.

- **Open input**: add `Candidate.facts` (a tuple of pairs) and pass a populated `ctx` (providers' pre-computed signals) at both call sites. Today it is `{}`.
- **Reuse**: `FILTERS` become `constraint` providers (with a `can_wait` flag so a held item is reported, not dropped). `KEYS` become `cost-term` providers (lexicographic in greedy-v1, weighted-capped in v2). `[schedule] resources` is already the `resource` seam, so `env:staging` capacity is a config row.
- **Explain**: `explain(placement)` lists every provider contribution by name, kind and value. This extends the itemised `terms` already in `Placement`.
- **Simulate**: OPT-simulate gets a provider on/off switch by name. Providers must be pure over (state-as-of, cfg), which also gives determinism.
- **Safety**: weights, caps (30 percent) and the makespan guard (+10 percent) come from `D-optimizer-answers`. A provider that raises is skipped and reported as `unavailable`. The round falls back to v1 if the guard trips.
- **Flow signals**: replace the fixed `Signals` fields with a `SIGNALS` registry (compute, threshold knob, minimum history, note). `as_signals` and `history_notes` iterate it.

### (d) Proposal registry

One proposal record (resolve `proposal.toml` against B-prop-model into one shape). A `ProposalKind` registry holds:

- fields and a validator
- `preview` text
- an `apply` that calls the owning verb (config set, task add, plan revision, unite request)
- a risk class
- a fingerprint for decline memory
- who may accept (person-only by default)

The `type` choices in `proposal.toml` become derived from the registry. Accept creates a plan revision, task, config change or unite request. Decline is remembered by fingerprint. Ranking and backpressure reuse B-sched-backpressure.

LK suggestions stay a peer-to-peer handoff, because their addressee is a lane and not the operator. They reuse the same `apply` interface. Do not merge the two records.

### (e) Notice registry

`NoticeKind(reason, order, template, fence, coalesce_key, rate_knob, next_call_cli, next_call_mcp)`. This replaces `REASONS` and the brief-section dicts. `next_call_*` is required, which satisfies `r-tell-dont-discover` and is checked by a test over every registered notice.

### (f) Predicate and class registry

One signature `(PredCtx) -> (ok, reason)`. The same registry serves `applies_when`, the approvals `Rule.when`, `Tick.enabled`, `by_class` joins and detector enablement. Classes (change class, risk class, environment class) are data rows with an ordered level, used by tighten-only layering.

Approval sites and standing rules move to manifest rows (`[[approval.site]]`, `[[approval.rule]]`). A plugin may add a site only at a tier at least as strict as the natural tier. It may not lower an existing tier. Any rule it adds ships OFF, as `policy.py` documents for today's rules.

### (g) Section registries

One `Section(surface, name, order, budget_share, build(ctx), knob, more_hint)` for brief, doctor notes, report, metrics views and detectors.

Detectors reuse P-observe.detectors as the registry owner. Do not make a second one. Provide the common `Provider` base only.

### (h) Conventions

- Directory: `ddflow/features/<name>.toml`, with code under the domain's own package.
- Sorted deterministic scan; duplicate-name error.
- A per-feature docs page, `docs/ddflow/features/<name>.md`, found by listing the directory (the pattern ports already use).
- A per-feature conformance table in `tests/test_feature_<name>.py`.
- An "add-a-feature" recipe at `docs/ddflow/features/README.md`.

### (i) Meta conformance test

`tests/test_feature_modularity.py` follows `test_adapter_modularity.py`. In a temp package it creates one feature with a gate, a join rule, a signal, a proposal kind, a notice, a record kind, a knob and a report section. It asserts:

- the former shared files are byte-identical;
- `gate status` shows the gate;
- the optimizer `explain` lists the signal;
- the brief shows the notice;
- the report shows the section;
- `config --explain` shows the knob.

It also carries a shrink-only list of hub files (`README.md`, `config.py`, `model.py`, `mcp.py`, `defs.py`). A plan-lint warning fires when a new task's globs name a hub that has a registry.

### (j) Versioning, security, performance, isolation

- **Versioning**: a `contract` integer. A deprecated contract still loads and warns in `doctor`.
- **Security**: a plugin cannot widen permissions. Gates, joins and approval classes are tighten-only unless a person approves a revision. Third-party plugins are out of scope. The route is the out-of-process protocol in `P-extension-seams.process-protocol`, behind an operator allowlist.
- **Performance**: manifests are data, so discovery is `tomllib` only. The measured costs of eager import are 76 ms for 49 config sections and 0.585 s for 31 declared families. Code stays behind `Lazy`. Add a startup-cost test under the B-perf-* budgets.
- **Isolation**: any provider, runner or section that errors is skipped, reported by name, and never fails the host command.

### What must NOT be made generic (YAGNI)

- The event fold stays closed (`HANDLERS`). The `registry.py` docstring says so; only declaration is derived.
- No weighted join in the first cut.
- No second scheduler or simulator.
- No third-party in-process plugins, no pluggy.
- Gate order within a stage is not a registry; the stage model owns it.

## Ordering that avoids rework

Wave A (land first, small):
1. LK-config-autodiscover (merged with DX-registry-remaining) and LK-events-autodiscover. Both remove existing shared-file serialization, and every later task adds knobs or event kinds.
2. EX-contract.

Wave B (the registries the phases consume):
3. EX-gate-plugins, then EX-join-policies together with WP-gate-stages. WP-gate-stages must not start before the `join` field is settled, or its stage model gets rewritten.
4. EX-predicates, EX-notices, EX-sections.
5. ADP-optimizer-followup, then EX-providers, before OPT-signals and OPT-order-v2.
6. Decide the proposal shape, then EX-proposals, before SCH-review-inbox, PM-review-job, WP-merge-propose and P-observe.proposals.

Wave C (the phase tasks, now each a manifest):
7. QA-gate-wire, QA-agent, LK-sg-*, WP-plan-record, WP-gate-fork, the TM, AR, PO and PM tasks, and MR-/CHG- when filed.
8. EX-approval-rows before any CHG or TM-safety approval site.

Close with EX-meta-test and EX-migrate-proof as soon as a registry exists. They prove the contract on real code rather than only on the throwaway.

## Decisions for the operator

1. **One feature manifest per feature, or per-surface directories only?** Recommended: a TOML manifest (`ddflow/features/<name>.toml`) that wires lazily, keeping the existing per-domain directories. A feature then costs one file without moving anything.
2. **One proposal record?** Recommended: yes. Resolve `proposal.toml` and B-prop-model into one shape before SCH-review-inbox, PM-review-job and WP-merge-propose start.
3. **Open an optimizer `ctx` and `Candidate.facts` now, before OPT-signals?** Recommended: yes, as EX-providers behind ADP-optimizer-followup. It avoids a v2 rewrite.
4. **Join policy defaults?** Recommended: `all`, with `any_of`, `quorum` and `by_class` available but tighten-only without approval. No `weighted` yet.
5. **Third-party plugins?** Recommended: out of scope. Revisit only through the out-of-process protocol and an allowlist.
6. **Phase placement?** Recommended: extend P-extension-seams rather than opening P-extensibility.

<result># R-audit-ux: usability and functionality audit (ddflow 0.2.10, 2026-11-03)

Facts are graded [V] measured or used by me, and [K] from memory. The research note R-audit-ux is filed with verdict CONFIRMED.

Measurement caveats:
- Load average was 64–70 on the machine, so the big-project timings are inflated.
- The scratch project is an idle-ish path (1 to 1.7 s).
- I did not run the full test suite.
- I did not drive the MCP server live. Token figures come from `ddflow doctor` and from byte counts divided by 4.
- Transcript counts cover 61 recent session files, which are mostly subagents driving the CLI through Bash.

## Summary

1. A new operator can reach a merged task in about 11 commands at about 1.2 s each [V]. They fall off the happy path at four points: three entry points (`init`, `adopt`, `onboard`); a 10-gate pipeline for a trivial task; no discovery verbs (`tour`, `next-steps`, `why`, `explain` and `completion` all return "invalid choice") [V]; and a 470 KB README as the only getting-started [V].
2. The structural usability problem is cost. Every call re-reads the log, and every cheap command is already about 1.1 s idle, because `--version` alone takes 1.12 s. On the real project (132,275 events, 116 MB, 831 shards) `brief` took 35 s, `status` 24.6 s, `next` 7.2 s and `show` 6.4 s under load [V].
3. For agents, session start costs 9,539 tokens in the `lean` profile (tools/list 8,592, instructions 674, brief 173 on an empty project) [V]. Real agents mostly bypass MCP: the 61 transcripts hold 34 MCP calls against thousands of Bash `ddflow` calls [V].
4. Refusals are well written. `complete` names every unmet gate plus the exact fix and approval route [V]. But they are not logged as events, so repeat refusals cannot be mined, and typo hints sit after a 3 KB command dump [V].
5. Most of what I would propose is already planned and open: OD-* (operator queue), NS-help-suggest, NS-recipes, NS-next-actions, COMP-*, B-org-*, LF-*, PM-report-*, SM-gh-import. The gap is mostly a thin first-success layer, a latency fix and a rewritten doc entry path, not new subsystems.

## 2. Operator journey notes

- **What is waiting for me.** `brief` tells the operator that 3 approvals wait, with the `approvals approve ID` command. That is good. There is no consolidated inbox: the OD-* chain is mostly open (OD-queue and OD-inventory are done; OD-cli, OD-digest, OD-brief, OD-seen, OD-sinks and OD-mcp are open).
- **Approvals.** `approvals pending`, `show`, `ask`, `attest`, `approve` and `deny` exist. The ask/attest help is bare. The `doctor` note says chat answers are read from a transcript the agent's user can edit, so they show only that a person answered. The remote relay (NS-attest-remote, NS-ask-mcp, NS-decide) is open.
- **Why blocked.** `next` explains blockers inline (README states "why everything else is blocked"). There is no single-item `why`/`explain`.
- **Finding records.** `search`, `recall`, `similar`, `dupes` and `history` exist. That is a strength for finding; the weakness is that every call re-folds the log.
- **Undo.** `upgrade --restore`, `replay` and `recover` exist. I found no top-level "undo last action" or "restore a removed record" verb on the CLI; the rule r-everything-managed says definitions are restorable. I did not verify the path end to end.
- **Crash recovery.** The `brief` opens with "RESUME: recoverable work found" and lists 5 of 10 crashed worktrees. That is an excellent first line. But it lists them five at a time, and 40 more have nothing to salvage. For an operator it is alarming noise without a single "clean these up" action.
- **Config.** `config --explain` exists with provenance such as `[file]` and `[default]`. It has no key filter that I could find.

## 4. Documentation

- README.md is 470,368 bytes and 6,933 lines, which is about 117,000 tokens. It mixes marketing, a "How do I" table whose cells are 300 to 700 characters, reference, rationale and testing notes.
- The first run is a good 10 lines (lines 154 to 179). But the README says "tell your agent implement phase P1", and the pipeline then has 10 gates. A new reader does not learn why.
- `docs/` has 315 files with no tutorial or "start here". There are separate HANDOFF, BACKLOG, RECOVERY, RESEARCH and ARCHITECTURE files.
- Audience coverage:

| Audience | Getting-started | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Operator | Partial | README "A first run"; help topic `manual` |
| Agent | Good | README "Instruction for an agent reader" plus generated drivers |
| Company admin | Missing | B-org-* are open |
| Contributor | Partial | README "Testing"; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md |

- Help topics: cli, config, customise, export, gates, import, lanes, manual, mcp, memory, metrics, parallel, recovery, upgrade, verify, workflow. There is no `quickstart`, `operator` or `faq` topic, and `help nonexistent` lists the topics but exits 1 (reasonable).
- `ddflow docs check` exists, and DX-docs-check-speed was just completed. I did not run it, since it is slow under this load.

## 5. Output accessibility

- `--json` exists on reads and carries `schema: "status@1"`, `"next@1"`. It works as either a global or a per-command flag (`ddflow --json status` and `ddflow status --json` both worked) [V].
- Exit codes are documented in the README and the agent section (0/1/2/3) [V]. rc=2 for "nothing ready" is deliberate, but a new human reads it as an error.
- `board` renders a markdown table with unicode progress bars and a gate-column legend. It is generated, fine for chat, and wide for a narrow terminal.
- I did not test `NO_COLOR` or `--no-color`, and found no mention of either in the help I read. Treat colour as unverified.
- There is no shell completion: all `COMP-*` except COMP-tree and COMP-ids-fast are open.

## 6. Defaults [V on scratch]

- Gates are on by default: research, rules, implement, rubber_duck, critic, standards, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, merge. `complete` refuses unless each carries an outcome.
- `evidence_required` makes `research` need evidence to pass [V].
- No reviewer is configured in a fresh project. The honest path is to record `unavailable`, but then `complete` also demands the "reviewer independence" condition and an author model. A fresh user with no reviewer key can hit a dead end except through `--force` (which agents may not use) or approvals. I did not drive that to the end.
- `gate skip` of a non-review gate needs no approval and takes a one-letter reason [V]. That is a loophole in the honesty story.
- `adopt --agents` defaults to ALL 24 listed agents [V from help]. For a user with one agent that is a lot of writes into their repo. Confirm whether it writes files for agents the user does not have.
- `merge` does not check gates [V]. The README says `complete` is the gate.

## 7. Discoverability

- 80 top-level commands in one flat, unordered alphabet-less list, about 100 families and 60+ phases. `ddflow --help` shows no grouping (Plan / Work / Review / Learn / Operate / Admin).
- Nothing tells a user which 8 of the 80 to learn first. The README "How do I" table does, but at 470 KB.
- Missing verbs: `tour`, `next-steps`, `why`, `explain` [V].

## 8. Observability of ddflow itself

- `doctor` is good: it states the session-start cost (9,539 of 40,000 budget), the index state, and approval-security caveats.
- False positives seen: two git-identity notes caused by my own test setup (arguably correct), the 8-line note block on a clean project, and "onboard status" returning rc=1 for expected-absent items.
- Missing: refusal events, command timing, and CLI latency per command. PM-selfcost and PM-report-* exist as plan.
- Telemetry: none; the PM-* telemetry work is local. I found no opt-in upload design. clig.dev requires consent first.

## 9. Idea to deployed with only ddflow today

- Idea to tasks: `plan`, `phase add`, `task add`, `import`. Works.
- Tasks to merged: the claim/gate/merge/complete loop. Works; heavy.
- Merged to deployed: `version`, `promote` (environment branches), `pr`. These exist, but LF-* (lifecycle map, stage gates, feedback loop, handoffs, profiles) is all open.
- Operate and feedback: LF-feedback, LF-health, PM-report-* are open. That means the "team in a box" claim stops after merge. A user falls off at deploy and feedback.
- The company-admin path (B-org-*, 20-plus open items) is a plan only.

Guidance fetched:
- **clig.dev** [V]:
  - Lead with examples in help, and print concise help with an example when arguments are missing.
  - Suggest a correction when the user's intent is guessable, but ask before running it.
  - Disable colour when `NO_COLOR` is set, when the output is not a TTY, or with `--no-color`.
  - Offer `--json`.
  - Prompt for a "y" confirmation on dangerous actions and support `--no-input`.
  - Respond within 100 ms, and print something before slow work.
  - Do not phone home without consent; prefer opt-in.
  - The page gives no shell-completion guidance, so I treat that as outside what it covers.
- **Anthropic, Writing tools for agents** [V]:
  - Fewer, consolidated tools; do not simply wrap endpoints.
  - Concise vs detailed response formats (206 vs 72 tokens in its Slack example).
  - Paginate, filter and truncate, with Claude Code capping tool responses at 25,000 tokens by default.
  - Tell the agent how to narrow its next call.
  - Write actionable errors with examples.
  - Evaluate with realistic multi-step tasks and track tool errors.
- **Diataxis** [V, only the page's own summary]: four forms (tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanation), each serving a different user need. The page itself did not state a separation rule in the extract I got.

What ddflow gets right against these: actionable refusals, `--json` with versioned schemas, a documented four-code exit contract, response budgets (`brief` is capped), and a lean MCP profile. What it misses: example-led help, grouped commands, a sub-second CLI, and a first-success path under 5 minutes.

## 5. Questions for the operator (with recommended defaults)

1. **Should a lighter default pipeline ship for a new project?** Recommend yes: a `light` profile chosen at `init` with the full pipeline one command away. Today a trivial task needs 10 gate outcomes.
2. **May `merge` warn, or refuse, when required gates have no outcome?** Recommend warn plus a visible "merged, awaiting gates" state. A refusal would break the current flow, where gates are recorded after the merge.
3. **Is it acceptable to take `lease.renewed` out of the committed log into a local sidecar?** Recommend yes after UX-latency-profile confirms it is the dominant cost. It changes what a clone can see about liveness.
4. **How should a one-command front door be named?** Recommend `ddflow start`, keeping `init`, `adopt` and `onboard` as the underlying stages.
5. **Should `adopt` write files for only the agents it detects?** Recommend yes (detect, then confirm).
6. **Telemetry for ddflow's own improvement: local only, or an opt-in upload?** Recommend local only for now. If an upload is ever added, it must be off by default with a first-run prompt (clig.dev's opt-in advice).
7. **README split: do you accept a large README diff now, while other agents edit it?** Recommend a single-owner task with a frozen README during the split.
8. **Is rc=2 for "nothing ready" worth keeping for humans?** Recommend keeping it for scripts and printing a plain "Nothing to do. Next: ..." line for a TTY.

## Part 2: Concept and coherence

### 2.1 Core promise

1. A queue of phases and tasks with declared dependencies and file globs.
2. Parallel agents work in isolated git worktrees. Leases on globs prevent two agents from writing the same files.
3. Every task passes gates that cannot be passed by assertion: unavailable is never passed, one reviewer comes from another model family, and a bug closes only with a regression test that failed first.
4. Everything is an append-only log in the repo. Crashes lose nothing, and projections are rebuilt from it.
5. It runs identically over CLI and MCP, needs no shell, and is configurable by user and company.

### 2.2 Personas

| Solo developer, one subscription | Partly. The core loop works, but the gate load (mean 62 min of gates per merged item, a mix of review and CI minutes) is built for a fleet | gate data in 2.5 |

Real: leases with TTL (5400 s default), worktrees, lanes, the gate pipeline, reviewer independence, approvals (`ask.*` events, standing approval windows), recovery of crashed work (`recover`), doctor and loops findings.

Aspirational: swarm scheduling across remote lanes, autopilot, ETA, optimizer, governor, goals/principles, "replace a software team".

My read of `R-lifecycle` is that it covers about 14 stages through the topic tracks, but with no typed trace edges, zero requirement records, no per-project lifecycle profile and no stage-exit gate. Only the engineering-execution stages (implement, gate, review, merge, recover) have any real use. ### 2.7 Single points of failure

- **Operator:** one person approves, decides and runs the loop. Approval load rose to 80–90 asks/day, which cannot be sustained without more auto-approval policy.
- **Reviewer endpoints:** reviewer independence needs a second family. 169 critic and 170 rubber_duck unavailables show endpoint outages already occur. `DX-reviewer-failover` is open.
- **One machine:** load 58. The known blocker `B2efda94671` is that the CI gate cannot finish inside its 3600 s timeout on a loaded machine, and baseline-red auto-accept never triggers. The suite is about 24 minutes serial and 48 seconds with 48 xdist workers (from the project's memory notes [K]).
- **Event log growth:** 116 MB in 36 days is about 3.2 MB/day, or about 1.2 GB/year. A full `list task` fold takes about 8 s at 132k events under load, so at 10x (1.3M events) a cold read is roughly 80 s or more without snapshots. `snap-log-ceiling` and the snapshot work are open and are the right fix.
- **Cost per task in tokens:** not measurable from the log. This is a gap (`P-token-economy`, 7 of 40 done).

### 3.1 Landscape notes

- **Claude Code** [V]: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default, behind `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`. A lead spawns teammates, each with its own context. They share a task list with pending, in-progress and completed states, plus dependencies (a blocked task is not self-claimed). Claiming uses file locking. They message each other through JSON mailboxes. Hooks `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated` and `TaskCompleted` can reject with exit code 2, which is a minimal gate. The doc says plainly: "Two teammates editing the same file leads to overwrites. Break the work so each teammate owns a different set of files." Known limits: no session resume for in-process teammates, task status lag, one team per session, no nested teams, token cost scales linearly. Its managed "Code Review" (March 2026, Team and Enterprise, about $15–25 per PR per secondary sources [K]) comments but does not merge, approve or block.
- **Codex app** [K/secondary]: macOS app launched 2026-02-02, parallel threads on worktrees, "Automations" for scheduled background runs with a review queue, cloud triggers announced as upcoming. Included in ChatGPT paid plans.
- **GitHub Copilot / Agent HQ** [K/secondary, Oct 2025 announcement]: Mission Control for assigning and tracking agents from several vendors, admin control plane with allowed agents, model access, usage metrics, per-agent identity. This is the closest thing to enterprise governance and is a platform play.
- **Conductor** [K/secondary]: macOS GUI running Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in worktrees. Free tier plus Pro about $50/month.
- **Claude Squad** [K/secondary]: open-source tmux-based worktree manager, AGPL-3.0.
- **Vibe Kanban** [V]: kanban over agents in worktrees, Apache-2.0, 28.6k stars, and its README banner reads "Vibe Kanban is sunsetting". This is direct evidence that a worktree-plus-board layer is a fragile business when the vendors ship similar features.
- **Spec Kit** [V]: 146.3k stars. Commands constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement, converge; extensions (bug fixing, idea assessment), presets for organisational standards, workflows, bundles, catalogs. Closest peer to ddflow's spec stage and to company presets.

### 3.3 Honest read

**Genuinely differentiated and defensible:**
- File-glob leases. The Claude Code doc, as fetched, tells users to partition files by hand. That gap can close, but it has not.
- Mandatory cross-family review with explicit "unavailable, not passed" semantics. No vendor will build "use a competitor's model to review mine".
- The replayable, repo-resident event log and the regression-test-before-close rule. These are audit properties vendors do not have an incentive to provide.
- A no-shell mode where every command runs over chat.

**Behind:**
- Remote and hosted operation (Codex, Devin, Copilot all have it).
- Scheduling (Codex Automations).
- GUI and inbox UX.
- Onboarding: `uv tool install` from git, "not on PyPI yet", then `adopt`, `import`, config. Spec Kit has 146k stars and a one-command start.
- Observability of cost.

**Redundant with what vendors will ship in the next 12 months** [K]:
- native worktrees (already shipped)
- shared task lists with dependencies and claim locking (shipped, experimental)
- completion hooks (shipped)
- managed PR review (shipped)
- scheduled automations
- an admin control plane and per-agent identity (Agent HQ)
- plan modes and subagent/skill registries

**What ddflow should not build:**
- its own GUI or kanban board (Vibe Kanban is sunsetting)
- harness-by-harness lane drivers for every new agent beyond a data-driven template (it already carries 24 descriptors, with 7 more "fit" phases filed)
- its own scheduler, a daemon manager (`P-daemon`) and a swarm scheduler duplicating Actions and Codex automations
- a requirements/spec product to compete with Spec Kit, OpenSpec and Kiro. Import and export their formats instead (`P-sdd` already points this way)
- a general knowledge hub (`P-knowledge-hub`), memory (`P-agent-memory`) and a skills registry (`P-skills`), all of which vendors ship natively and which route through the same hub tasks

**Hype caution:** much of the 2026 landscape comes from vendor-run comparison blogs, and star counts conflict between sources. Treat the "replace a software company" ambition as marketing language for now. The only parts with usage evidence here are queue, lease, gate, review and recovery.

### 4.2 Release 1.0 definition

Release 1.0 is true when all of these hold:
1. A new user can install from PyPI, run `adopt`, and finish one task end to end in under 30 minutes with the default pipeline (default gates not needing a second family).
2. Median gate time per merged item is at most 20 minutes, the forced-completion share is under 5%, and a CI run cannot exceed its timeout on a loaded machine without a decided outcome.
3. Reads stay under 2 s at 1M events (snapshot-backed), with a documented archive path.
4. All config is in one layered stack (default, conf.d, org, local), every knob is searchable, and a company bundle works.
5. Every external dependency is behind a port (the `r-adapters` ratchet at zero violations).
6. The harness contract is data-driven, and 3 harnesses are tested for real (Claude Code, Codex, one more).
7. Open bug count under 20, and no crashed worktree older than 24 h.
8. Remote operation is documented, with a status for each mode (local CLI, local MCP, remote MCP).

Staged MVP slice per persona:

| Persona | Slice |
|---|---|
| Solo developer | queue, leases, worktrees, `review.max_rounds=1`, one reviewer, default pipeline of CI and critic only |
| Team lead | add fleet gates, recover, lanes, standing approvals |
| Company admin | add org bundle, graded policies, audit export |
| QA / researcher | import and export of existing test and research artifacts only |
| Cross-project | one pilot pair of sister repos with a manual manifest |

### 4.3 Scope controls

- **Intake:** the task-add hygiene (TA-*) already exists; make it blocking above WIP. New phases need a named user, a stated falsifier and a kill date.
- **WIP limit:** at most 8 open phases with running work and 20 open phases total; park the rest as `proposed`.
- **Architecture budget:** ratchets on config knobs (530 now; net-new knobs need a removed one), CLI verbs (88), MCP tools (137) and event kinds (66), set to the current value and enforced like the existing size guard.
- **Unproven tag:** every phase created after 10-20 gets an `unproven` tag with a review-by date 30 days out; if no item is done and no user named, it is abandoned.
- **Sunsetting:** a monthly cadence (`ddflow cadence`) that lists phases with zero completions in 30 days.
- **Self-repair ceiling:** if `fix-*` completions exceed 35% of throughput for two consecutive weeks, stop feature intake.

- **Atomic file writes** (`fsio.atomic_write`): temp file, fsync, rename, mode kept.

### Unverified suspicions (report only)

1. `fsio.atomic_write` and a new shard creation never fsync the parent directory. A crash after the rename can lose it on ext4. Low.
2. `_redact_data` falls back to the built-in patterns when the config is unreadable (`_eventlog.py:~363`). Custom `redact_patterns` are then skipped for that write, which fails open for custom secrets.
3. Approval requester binding compares `canon.agent`, a self-declared name (`as_agent`/`--agent`), so identity is unauthenticated. The digest binding limits the impact. GR-identity is related.
4. The PreToolUse lease check uses `CK.paths_of(raw)` (file-path tools). Bash writes (`sed -i`, `>`, `tee`) are not lease-checked.
5. The hook is fail-open on any error (`api/setup/hooks.py:352`, by design) and so is Bash `forbidden` on a `Config.load` failure.
6. Nine product `shutil.rmtree` sites have no guard. The cwd-delete guard from Be5e7dc7e27 lives only in `tests/safe_cleanup.py`. [V] `shutil.rmtree(Path(""), ignore_errors=True)` empties the cwd. Reachable only if a path variable is empty:
   - `services/lane_headless.py:304`
   - `services/ci/scratch.py:69`
   - `services/cleanup/actions.py:57`
   - `services/backups.py:113,261`
   - `services/swarm/lanehooks.py:302`
   - `infra/worktree/_create.py:27`
   - `services/upgrade_dryrun/_drive.py:28`
   - `_steps.py:78`
7. `surfaces/mcp/_offload.py:~110`: if `p.stdin.write` raises `BrokenPipe`, the worker `p` is neither killed nor waited for, so the process leaks. The worker log is opened without an encoding.
8. The FTS5 `words` quoting in `infra/docindex.py:365` is untested for a word containing `"`.
9. Case-insensitive filesystems: shards `A.jsonl` and `a.jsonl` collide in git.
10. The ruff target is `py311`, but `PLW1510` is ignored globally. A subprocess caller can forget `check=` everywhere.
11. Open bugs not mine: B-mcp-no-type-enum-check (MCP type, enum and range validation) and B-review-chunk-timeout-not-enforced (review chunk request outlives its `timeout_s` cut). I did not re-file them.

### Performance

- [V] 132,214 events, 116 MB under `.ddflow/events`, in 831 shards.
- The CLI start cost is imports, not fold, so the fix is lazy imports (Bb90f72f770). I did not measure fold cost on the full log.

data.text: Make a research to extend and make compliant the ability for this project (and also as a project rule) that every feature should be supported to work locally, or via mcp (keeping the mcp tools as small as possible) and support working with local access, or without local access, with minimized token usage, help and suggestions for the commands to help the LLM, ability to operate in docker container (aka devcontainer), or ddflow in a docker container without fs access, or work as a remote mcp server. We would like to be able for ddflow project to be able to be integrated with external TUI, and GUI, boards, provided by other tools and third party, so from architecture point of view this has to be assumed and taken when a design or feature is built for ddflow

data.decision: OPERATOR 2026-11-03: external TUI, GUI and board front ends from other tools and third parties must be able to integrate with ddflow. ddflow itself ships no GUI (D-scope-focus-2026-11), but every design and feature assumes an external front end: all state and actions are reachable through a stable, versioned, documented machine interface (JSON schemas, events/subscriptions, MCP, and a local or remote API), never only as human text or CLI prose; views are derived data with schema ids; actions return structured results with next-call hints; changes can be streamed; identity, consent and approvals work for a non-agent client.

fields.body: Decision D-external-frontends. RULE: a feature is not done until a third-party front end can read its state and invoke its actions without scraping text: a versioned JSON schema (schema id) for every view and result, structured refusals with the next call, a way to follow changes (event feed or subscription) instead of polling the whole log, ids and links that are stable, pagination and size caps, and approvals, consent and identity that work for a human client as well as an agent. Presentation (colour, tables, prose) is a thin layer over the data and never the only form. ddflow ships no GUI of its own. CHECK: a surface-parity test that every CLI/MCP view has a registered JSON schema and a version; a conformance suite a third-party client can run.
